  periodic `v`, via Mathlib's `UnitAddTorus.hasSum_sq_mFourierCoeff`), `torusCoeff_imag_shift` (coefficients of
  `x ↦ g(x+it)` are `ĝ_k e^{-2π k·t}`), `sum_sq_torusCoeff_shift_le`, `sum_sq_torusCoeff_exp_le` (corner sum,

- `KAM/Strip/CohomologicalParsevalLattice.lean` (116): `cohConstP`, `cohConstP_nonneg`, `cohConstP_pos`

- `KAM/Strip/CohomologicalParsevalBound.lean` (131): `norm_cohSolution_parseval_le` (scalar pointwise bound).
- `KAM/Strip/CohomologicalParseval.lean` (289): vector/matrix/a-priori transfers (`norm_cohSolutionPi_parseval_le`,

## Approach
`cohConstP n τ = (2π)⁻¹ √(2ⁿ (2τ/(eπ))^{2τ} (8n/π)ⁿ)`. Bessel on each corner shift, summed over the 2ⁿ sign
vectors (finite sets of modes, no tsum interchange); Cauchy–Schwarz on a finite set; `m^{2τ}e^{-2πδm} ≤
(2τ/(eπδ))^{2τ} e^{-πδm}` then the existing `tsum_exp_neg_modeSize_ne_zero_le`. **No `δ ≤ 1` is needed**; the
theorems have exactly the premises of `KAM.cohomological` / `KAM.cohomological_operator`. The existing files
were not edited; the matrix/a-priori derivations are re-proved verbatim against `cohConstP`.
The Mathlib route was cheaper than a direct orthonormality proof. Mathlib's torus file uses a file-local
`MeasureSpace UnitAddCircle := ⟨AddCircle.haarAddCircle⟩`; the Bessel file declares the same local instances.

## Numeric comparison (python)
`cohConstP 2 1 = 0.37967`, `cohConst 2 1 = 0.48341` (the constant is smaller too, though the real gain is the
exponent: `δ^{-(τ+n/2)}` versus `δ^{-(τ+n)}`).
